title: Dileram's Sons Send Their Wealth to Kasur

blocks.text: Dileram's household tries to save itself by scattering valuables before the Khalsa closes in. His sons in Lahore transferred all their assets to Kasur, sending ornaments, cash, and dependents away for protection, but the move itself exposes how fear and hurried transport are already unraveling the family estate.

The poem then turns back to Dileram's haveli, where the first wave of plunder strips away what lies openly at hand and rough opportunists are pushed aside by stronger claimants. What seemed like an ordinary sack quickly becomes a more methodical search for hidden or buried treasure inside the mansion.

By the end of the page the conflict is no longer only about punishing a political enemy. The chiefs and returning soldiers realize that Dileram's wealth may be immense, and the hunt for concealed stores begins to govern the entire episode.
